title: Quantification of Appetitive and Mechanical Aversive Learning in Drosophila via Y-maze Assay
author: Mabry, Malgireddy, et al.
materials: Flystuff Drosophila CO2 fly pad (Genesee Scientific #59‐114)
Use double‐distilled, deionized water unless otherwise specified.

Both Basic Protocols 1 and 2 are organized to ensure a defined order for conditioned odor and stimulus pairing. However, in our experience, the order of stimulus pairing does not significantly alter the outcome of the experiment. Ultimately, it is important to conduct both stimulus‐pairing orders as a control (e.g., pair the odor with the vortex first, then pair the second neutral odor). Furthermore, it is crucial to always split the trials so that half are associated with one odor (e.g., IAA) and the other half with the other (e.g., EA) to ensure no bias toward one odor over the other.

steps.title: Make 1% agar starvation vials
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1% agar solution in double‑distilled/deionized water, boil until fully dissolved, dispense 5 mL into each narrow polypropylene Drosophila vial, let solidify for 1–2 h, remove excess condensation; if not used immediately, refrigerate and use within 1 week, discard any vial where agar has dried or pulled away from the walls.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1% agar solution in double‑distilled/deionized water.
Boil until agar is completely dissolved.
Add 5 mL of the hot agar to each narrow polypropylene vial.
Allow the agar to solidify for 1–2 h.
Remove excess condensation before adding flies.
If not used promptly, refrigerate and use within 1 week; discard if agar dries from vial walls.

steps.title: Prepare sucrose‑supplemented medium
steps.instruction: Microwave fly food for approximately 30 seconds, cool until warm to the touch, add sucrose to reach a final 1 M concentration, mix thoroughly, dispense 5 mL into each narrow polypropylene vial, allow 1–2 h to solidify, remove condensation and use the vials the same day.

substeps.instruction: Microwave the fly food for ~30 s.
Cool the food until it is warm to the touch.
Add sucrose to achieve a final concentration of 1 M.
Mix thoroughly.
Add 5 mL of the sucrose‑supplemented food to each narrow polypropylene vial.
Allow the food to solidify for 1–2 h.
Remove excess condensation before adding flies; use the vials the same day.

steps.title: Prepare odor solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute ethyl acetate (EA) in mineral oil at a 1:50 ratio and isoamyl alcohol (IAA) in mineral oil at a 1:100 ratio; make both solutions fresh before each experiment.

substeps.instruction: Dilute EA in mineral oil 1:50 (v/v).
Dilute IAA in mineral oil 1:100 (v/v).
Prepare fresh solutions immediately prior to each assay.

steps.title: Assemble Y‑maze apparatus
steps.instruction: Place the small plastic funnel into the 20‑mL glass beaker at the bottom of the Y‑maze so that no flies can escape; trim the funnel slightly if necessary to achieve a snug fit.

substeps.instruction: Insert the small plastic funnel into the 20‑mL beaker.
Ensure the funnel sits flush with the beaker bottom, preventing escape routes.
If needed, cut the funnel slightly for an ideal fit.

steps.title: Handle flies without CO₂
steps.instruction: Do not expose flies to CO₂ on the experimental day; if flies have previously been anesthetized with CO₂, wait 16–20 h after the last exposure before beginning the Y‑maze assay.

steps.title: Starve flies (Basic Protocol 2)
steps.instruction: Transfer flies into the prepared 1% agar starvation vials and starve for an overnight period of 18–20 h; afterwards feed them the 1 M sucrose‑supplemented medium.

substeps.instruction: Place flies into the 1% agar starvation vials.
Starve for 18–20 h (overnight).
After starvation, provide the 1 M sucrose‑supplemented fly medium.

steps.title: Condition flies with odor‑stimulus pairing
steps.instruction: For each trial, pair one odor (IAA or EA) with the mechanical vortex stimulus (using the analog vortex mixer for Basic Protocol 2) and the other odor with no stimulus; conduct both pairing orders as controls, splitting trials evenly between the two odors to avoid bias; use a timer for Basic Protocol 1 to time each pairing.

substeps.instruction: Select the odor to be paired with the vortex stimulus for the current trial.
Apply the mechanical vortex stimulus using the analog vortex mixer (Basic Protocol 2).
Present the opposite odor without stimulus in the same trial.
Repeat the procedure with the opposite pairing order in a separate set of trials.
Ensure that half of all trials use IAA and half use EA.
Use a timer (Basic Protocol 1) to control the duration of each pairing.

steps.title: Test flies in Y‑maze
steps.instruction: Introduce conditioned flies into the Y‑maze under light conditions during their subjective day, run 8–12 trials per assay, record the arm choice for each fly, and complete testing within 3–4 h.

substeps.instruction: Place flies into the Y‑maze apparatus under light conditions during their subjective day.
Run 8–12 choice trials per assay.
Record the arm chosen by each fly.
Finish the entire testing session within 3–4 h.

steps.title: Clean and store apparatus
steps.instruction: Rinse all components (Falcon tubes, pipette tips, Y‑maze parts) thoroughly with water, avoid odorous cleaners such as ethanol, and allow all parts to dry overnight before the next use.

substeps.instruction: Rinse each part of the apparatus with water.
Do not use odorous cleaning agents (e.g., ethanol).
Allow all cleaned parts to dry completely overnight.
Store the dried components for future assays.
